import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Parshin's conjecture

Parshin's conjecture (also called the Beilinson–Parshin conjecture) states that for every
smooth projective variety $X$ over a finite field, the higher algebraic K-groups of $X$
vanish up to torsion: $K_i(X) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = 0$ for all $i > 0$.

Mathlib has no definition of higher algebraic K-theory, so this file constructs the
algebraic K-groups of a scheme from scratch, following Waldhausen:

* `IsVectorBundle X M` says that the sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules `M` is locally free of
  finite rank. The full subcategory of `X.Modules` on these objects, together with the short
  exact sequences of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules, is the exact category of vector bundles on $X$.
* For an abelian category `A` and a property `P` of objects of `A` (thought of as an exact
  subcategory of `A`), `sConstruction P : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ ⥤ Cat` is Waldhausen's
  $S_\bullet$-construction: `S_n P` is the category of functors `Ar[n] ⥤ A` sending
  `(i, j)` to an object `F(i, j)` satisfying `P`, with `F(i, i)` zero and with
  `F(i, j) → F(i, k) → F(j, k)` short exact for all `i ≤ j ≤ k`.
* `kSpace P` is the geometric realization $|iS_\bullet P|$ of the bisimplicial set
  $N_\bullet iS_\bullet P$ whose $(n, k)$-simplices are strings of $k$ composable
  isomorphisms in $S_n P$. Waldhausen's K-theory space is the loop space
  $\Omega |iS_\bullet P|$, so that `KGroup P _ i` is $K_i(P) = \pi_{i+1}(|iS_\bullet P|, ∗)$
  with base point the zero object. For an exact category this agrees with Quillen's
  K-theory by Waldhausen's comparison theorem [Wa85, §1.9].
* `algebraicKGroup X i` is the `i`-th algebraic K-group $K_i(X)$ of the scheme `X`, namely
  the `i`-th K-group of the exact category of vector bundles on `X`.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Parshin's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parshin%27s_conjecture)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* [Wa85] F. Waldhausen, *Algebraic K-theory of spaces*, Lecture Notes in Math. 1126 (1985),
  318–419.
* [Ka05] B. Kahn, *Algebraic K-theory, algebraic cycles and arithmetic geometry*,
  Handbook of K-theory I, Springer (2005).
-/

blocks.name: arrowOfLE
blocks.text:
/-- The object `(i, j)` of the arrow category `Ar[n]` of the poset `[n] = {0 < 1 < ⋯ < n}`,
for `i ≤ j`. -/
abbrev arrowOfLE {n : ℕ} {i j : Fin (n + 1)} (h : i ≤ j) : Arrow (Fin (n + 1)) :=
  Arrow.mk (homOfLE h)

blocks.code:
structure IsSObj (P : ObjectProperty A) {n : ℕ} (F : Arrow (Fin (n + 1)) ⥤ A) : Prop where
  /-- Every value `F(i, j)` satisfies `P`. -/
  prop : ∀ a, P (F.obj a)
  /-- The values `F(i, i)` on the diagonal are zero objects. -/
  isZero : ∀ i : Fin (n + 1), IsZero (F.obj (arrowOfLE (le_refl i)))
  /-- For `i ≤ j ≤ k`, the sequence `F(i, j) → F(i, k) → F(j, k)` is short exact. -/
  shortExact : ∀ (i j k : Fin (n + 1)) (hij : i ≤ j) (hjk : j ≤ k),
    ∃ w, (ShortComplex.mk
      (F.map (Arrow.homMk (f := arrowOfLE hij) (g := arrowOfLE (hij.trans hjk))
        (𝟙 i) (homOfLE hjk) (Subsingleton.elim _ _)))
      (F.map (Arrow.homMk (f := arrowOfLE (hij.trans hjk)) (g := arrowOfLE hjk)
        (homOfLE hij) (𝟙 k) (Subsingleton.elim _ _))) w).ShortExact
blocks.docstring:
A functor `F : Ar[n] ⥤ A` is an object of Waldhausen's `S_n P` if all its values `F(i, j)`
satisfy `P`, its values `F(i, i)` on the diagonal are zero objects, and for all `i ≤ j ≤ k` the
sequence `F(i, j) → F(i, k) → F(j, k)` is a short exact sequence in `A`.

blocks.name: IsSObj
blocks.text:
/-- A functor `F : Ar[n] ⥤ A` is an object of Waldhausen's `S_n P` if all its values `F(i, j)`
satisfy `P`, its values `F(i, i)` on the diagonal are zero objects, and for all `i ≤ j ≤ k` the
sequence `F(i, j) → F(i, k) → F(j, k)` is a short exact sequence in `A`. -/
structure IsSObj (P : ObjectProperty A) {n : ℕ} (F : Arrow (Fin (n + 1)) ⥤ A) : Prop where
  /-- Every value `F(i, j)` satisfies `P`. -/
  prop : ∀ a, P (F.obj a)
  /-- The values `F(i, i)` on the diagonal are zero objects. -/
  isZero : ∀ i : Fin (n + 1), IsZero (F.obj (arrowOfLE (le_refl i)))
  /-- For `i ≤ j ≤ k`, the sequence `F(i, j) → F(i, k) → F(j, k)` is short exact. -/
  shortExact : ∀ (i j k : Fin (n + 1)) (hij : i ≤ j) (hjk : j ≤ k),
    ∃ w, (ShortComplex.mk
      (F.map (Arrow.homMk (f := arrowOfLE hij) (g := arrowOfLE (hij.trans hjk))
        (𝟙 i) (homOfLE hjk) (Subsingleton.elim _ _)))
      (F.map (Arrow.homMk (f := arrowOfLE (hij.trans hjk)) (g := arrowOfLE hjk)
        (homOfLE hij) (𝟙 k) (Subsingleton.elim _ _))) w).ShortExact
variable (P : ObjectProperty A)

blocks.code:
def sProp (n : SimplexCategory) : ObjectProperty (Arrow (Fin (n.len + 1)) ⥤ A) :=
  fun F => IsSObj P F
blocks.docstring: The objects of `S_n P`, as a property of functors `Ar[n] ⥤ A`.

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 18 19]
lemma IsSObj.comp {m n : SimplexCategory} (θ : m ⟶ n) {F : Arrow (Fin (n.len + 1)) ⥤ A}
    (hF : IsSObj P F) : IsSObj P (θ.toOrderHom.monotone.functor.mapArrow ⋙ F) where
  prop _ := hF.prop _
  isZero i := hF.isZero (θ.toOrderHom i)
  shortExact _ _ _ hij hjk :=
    hF.shortExact _ _ _ (θ.toOrderHom.monotone hij) (θ.toOrderHom.monotone hjk)
blocks.docstring:
The property `IsSObj P` is stable under precomposition with the functor `Ar[m] ⥤ Ar[n]`
induced by a monotone map `θ : [m] → [n]`; this gives the simplicial structure of `S_• P`.
blocks.name: IsSObj.comp
blocks.text:
/-- The property `IsSObj P` is stable under precomposition with the functor `Ar[m] ⥤ Ar[n]`
induced by a monotone map `θ : [m] → [n]`; this gives the simplicial structure of `S_• P`. -/
@[category API, AMS 18 19]
lemma IsSObj.comp {m n : SimplexCategory} (θ : m ⟶ n) {F : Arrow (Fin (n.len + 1)) ⥤ A}
    (hF : IsSObj P F) : IsSObj P (θ.toOrderHom.monotone.functor.mapArrow ⋙ F) where
  prop _ := hF.prop _
  isZero i := hF.isZero (θ.toOrderHom i)
  shortExact _ _ _ hij hjk :=
    hF.shortExact _ _ _ (θ.toOrderHom.monotone hij) (θ.toOrderHom.monotone hjk)

blocks.code:
def sConstruction : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ ⥤ Cat where
  obj n := Cat.of (sProp P n.unop).FullSubcategory
  map θ := Functor.toCatHom <| (sProp P _).lift ((sProp P _).ι ⋙
    (Functor.whiskeringLeft _ _ A).obj θ.unop.toOrderHom.monotone.functor.mapArrow)
    (fun F => F.2.comp P θ.unop)
  map_id _ := rfl
  map_comp _ _ := rfl
blocks.docstring:
Waldhausen's `S_•`-construction of `P`, as a simplicial category: `S_n P` is the full
subcategory of `Ar[n] ⥤ A` on the objects satisfying `IsSObj P`, and a monotone map
`θ : [m] → [n]` acts by precomposition with the induced functor `Ar[m] ⥤ Ar[n]`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib `CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.ShortExact`, `Arrow`, `ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory`, `SimplexCategory` (used as building blocks); no K-theoretic construction exists in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib.
justification.name: IsSObj / sProp / sConstruction (with helper arrowOfLE and API lemma IsSObj.comp)
justification.why_needed: Waldhausen's S_•-construction of an exact (sub)category P of an abelian category A, as a functor SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ ⥤ Cat; Mathlib has no S_•-construction, Q-construction or exact categories.

blocks.name: sConstruction
blocks.text:
/-- Waldhausen's `S_•`-construction of `P`, as a simplicial category: `S_n P` is the full
subcategory of `Ar[n] ⥤ A` on the objects satisfying `IsSObj P`, and a monotone map
`θ : [m] → [n]` acts by precomposition with the induced functor `Ar[m] ⥤ Ar[n]`. -/
def sConstruction : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ ⥤ Cat where
  obj n := Cat.of (sProp P n.unop).FullSubcategory
  map θ := Functor.toCatHom <| (sProp P _).lift ((sProp P _).ι ⋙
    (Functor.whiskeringLeft _ _ A).obj θ.unop.toOrderHom.monotone.functor.mapArrow)
    (fun F => F.2.comp P θ.unop)
  map_id _ := rfl
  map_comp _ _ := rfl
end SConstruction

/- ### Vector bundles and the algebraic K-theory of a scheme -/
section VectorBundles
variable (X : Scheme.{u})

blocks.code:
def IsVectorBundle (M : X.Modules) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : X, ∃ (U : X.Opens) (n : ℕ), x ∈ U ∧
    Nonempty (M.restrict U.ι ≅
      SheafOfModules.free (R := (U : Scheme.{u}).ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin n)))
blocks.docstring:
A sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules `M` is a vector bundle (i.e. locally free of finite rank) if
every point has an open neighbourhood `U` such that the restriction of `M` to `U` is
isomorphic to a free `𝒪_U`-module of some finite rank `n`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib `SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation`/`IsQuasicoherent` (not locally free); FormalConjecturesForMathlib `SheafOfModules.IsVectorBundleWithRank` (requires constant rank and extra site instances, used awkwardly in HartshorneConjecture.lean).
justification.name: IsVectorBundle
justification.why_needed: Locally free sheaves of 𝒪_X-modules of finite rank on a scheme; Mathlib has no such notion for sheaves of modules.

blocks.name: IsVectorBundle
blocks.text:
/-- A sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules `M` is a vector bundle (i.e. locally free of finite rank) if
every point has an open neighbourhood `U` such that the restriction of `M` to `U` is
isomorphic to a free `𝒪_U`-module of some finite rank `n`. -/
def IsVectorBundle (M : X.Modules) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : X, ∃ (U : X.Opens) (n : ℕ), x ∈ U ∧
    Nonempty (M.restrict U.ι ≅
      SheafOfModules.free (R := (U : Scheme.{u}).ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin n)))

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem isVectorBundle_zero : IsVectorBundle X 0 :=
  fun _ => ⟨⊤, 0, trivial, ⟨IsZero.iso
    ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor _).map_isZero (isZero_zero _))
    ((isColimitEquivIsInitialOfIsEmpty _ (colimit.cocone _) (colimit.isColimit _)).isZero)⟩⟩
blocks.docstring: The zero sheaf is a vector bundle (of rank `0`).

noncomputable abbrev algebraicKGroup (i : ℕ) : Type _ :=
  KGroup (IsVectorBundle X) (isVectorBundle_zero X) i

blocks.text:
/-- The `i`-th algebraic K-group `K_i(X)` of a scheme `X`, defined as the `i`-th K-group of the
exact category of vector bundles on `X` (with base point the zero vector bundle). -/
noncomputable abbrev algebraicKGroup (i : ℕ) : Type _ :=
  KGroup (IsVectorBundle X) (isVectorBundle_zero X) i
end VectorBundles

blocks.name: IsProjective
blocks.text:
/-- A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` is projective if it factors as a closed immersion
`X ⟶ ℙ^n_S` followed by the projection `ℙ^n_S ⟶ S`, for some `n`. -/
def IsProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (g : X ⟶ ℙ(Fin (n + 1); S)),
    IsClosedImmersion g ∧ CategoryStruct.comp g (pullback.fst _ _) = f

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 14]
lemma isProjective_projectiveSpace {S : Scheme.{u}} (n : ℕ) :

claims.decomposer_note: Single Prop with implicit universal quantifiers over every finite field k, every smooth projective k-variety X, and every degree i > 0 ('higher' means i ≥ 1, excluding K_0); 'vanish up to torsion' means K_i(X) ⊗ ℚ = 0, i.e. each K_i(X) is a torsion abelian group (the article's dim 0 and dim 1 cases are known results, not separate questions posed by the statement), and note Mathlib currently has no definition of higher algebraic K-theory, so the formalization will need substantial new infrastructure.
claims.reviewer_why: All four formalizing candidates (c01, c03, c04, c08) agree on the hypotheses (finite field k, integral scheme X, Mathlib `IsSmooth f`, bespoke projectivity = closed immersion into ℙⁿ_k followed by projection, i > 0) and conclusion (K_i(X) torsion ⟺ K_i(X) ⊗ ℚ = 0); they differ only in how the (Mathlib-absent) higher K-groups are built. c03/c04/c08 build K_i(X) = π_{i+1}(|iS_• Vect(X)|) via Waldhausen's S_•-construction on the exact category of vector bundles (locally free finite rank 𝒪_X-modules with the ambient short exact sequences), which is the textbook definition (agreeing with Quillen's K(P(X)) by Waldhausen §1.9). c01 uses Grayson's binary-multicomplex presentation, which I checked transcribes Grayson's Cor. 7.4 correctly but relies on a less standard theorem for identification with K_n. I chose c04 as the most literal and transparent encoding: S_n P as a full subcategory of Ar[n] ⥤ A (F(i,i) zero, F(i,j)→F(i,k)→F(j,k) short exact), simplicial object in Cat by precomposition, Mathlib `Core`, `nerveFunctor`, diagonal, `SSet.toTop`, `HomotopyGroup.Pi` at the canonical zero-object basepoint (with a proved API lemma that the zero sheaf is a vector bundle). c03 is equivalent but encodes the diagonal via a hand-rolled poset; c08 quantifies over all basepoints instead of constructing one (equivalent by path-connectedness but less canonical). Edits: made `k` explicit, added a `category test` lemma that ℙⁿ_S is projective over S (from c03) and a test that the higher K-groups are abelian groups, and clarified the torsion/⊗ℚ equivalence in the docstring.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Parshin's conjecture

Parshin's conjecture (also called the Beilinson–Parshin conjecture) states that for every
smooth projective variety $X$ over a finite field, the higher algebraic K-groups of $X$
vanish up to torsion: $K_i(X) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = 0$ for all $i > 0$.

Mathlib has no definition of higher algebraic K-theory, so this file constructs the
algebraic K-groups of a scheme from scratch, following Waldhausen:

* `IsVectorBundle X M` says that the sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules `M` is locally free of
  finite rank. The full subcategory of `X.Modules` on these objects, together with the short
  exact sequences of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules, is the exact category of vector bundles on $X$.
* For an abelian category `A` and a property `P` of objects of `A` (thought of as an exact
  subcategory of `A`), `sConstruction P : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ ⥤ Cat` is Waldhausen's
  $S_\bullet$-construction: `S_n P` is the category of functors `Ar[n] ⥤ A` sending
  `(i, j)` to an object `F(i, j)` satisfying `P`, with `F(i, i)` zero and with
  `F(i, j) → F(i, k) → F(j, k)` short exact for all `i ≤ j ≤ k`.
* `kSpace P` is the geometric realization $|iS_\bullet P|$ of the bisimplicial set
  $N_\bullet iS_\bullet P$ whose $(n, k)$-simplices are strings of $k$ composable
  isomorphisms in $S_n P$. Waldhausen's K-theory space is the loop space
  $\Omega |iS_\bullet P|$, so that `KGroup P _ i` is $K_i(P) = \pi_{i+1}(|iS_\bullet P|, ∗)$
  with base point the zero object. For an exact category this agrees with Quillen's
  K-theory by Waldhausen's comparison theorem [Wa85, §1.9].
* `algebraicKGroup X i` is the `i`-th algebraic K-group $K_i(X)$ of the scheme `X`, namely
  the `i`-th K-group of the exact category of vector bundles on `X`.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Parshin's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parshin%27s_conjecture)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* [Wa85] F. Waldhausen, *Algebraic K-theory of spaces*, Lecture Notes in Math. 1126 (1985),
  318–419.
* [Ka05] B. Kahn, *Algebraic K-theory, algebraic cycles and arithmetic geometry*,
  Handbook of K-theory I, Springer (2005).
-/

open CategoryTheory Limits AlgebraicGeometry Topology ZeroObject
open scoped Simplicial

namespace ParshinsConjecture

universe u v

/- ### Waldhausen's `S_•`-construction -/

section SConstruction

variable {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A]

/-- The object `(i, j)` of the arrow category `Ar[n]` of the poset `[n] = {0 < 1 < ⋯ < n}`,
for `i ≤ j`. -/
abbrev arrowOfLE {n : ℕ} {i j : Fin (n + 1)} (h : i ≤ j) : Arrow (Fin (n + 1)) :=
  Arrow.mk (homOfLE h)

/-- A functor `F : Ar[n] ⥤ A` is an object of Waldhausen's `S_n P` if all its values `F(i, j)`
satisfy `P`, its values `F(i, i)` on the diagonal are zero objects, and for all `i ≤ j ≤ k` the
sequence `F(i, j) → F(i, k) → F(j, k)` is a short exact sequence in `A`. -/
structure IsSObj (P : ObjectProperty A) {n : ℕ} (F : Arrow (Fin (n + 1)) ⥤ A) : Prop where
  /-- Every value `F(i, j)` satisfies `P`. -/
  prop : ∀ a, P (F.obj a)
  /-- The values `F(i, i)` on the diagonal are zero objects. -/
  isZero : ∀ i : Fin (n + 1), IsZero (F.obj (arrowOfLE (le_refl i)))
  /-- For `i ≤ j ≤ k`, the sequence `F(i, j) → F(i, k) → F(j, k)` is short exact. -/
  shortExact : ∀ (i j k : Fin (n + 1)) (hij : i ≤ j) (hjk : j ≤ k),
    ∃ w, (ShortComplex.mk
      (F.map (Arrow.homMk (f := arrowOfLE hij) (g := arrowOfLE (hij.trans hjk))
        (𝟙 i) (homOfLE hjk) (Subsingleton.elim _ _)))
      (F.map (Arrow.homMk (f := arrowOfLE (hij.trans hjk)) (g := arrowOfLE hjk)
        (homOfLE hij) (𝟙 k) (Subsingleton.elim _ _))) w).ShortExact

variable (P : ObjectProperty A)

/-- The objects of `S_n P`, as a property of functors `Ar[n] ⥤ A`. -/
def sProp (n : SimplexCategory) : ObjectProperty (Arrow (Fin (n.len + 1)) ⥤ A) :=
  fun F => IsSObj P F

/-- The property `IsSObj P` is stable under precomposition with the functor `Ar[m] ⥤ Ar[n]`
induced by a monotone map `θ : [m] → [n]`; this gives the simplicial structure of `S_• P`. -/
@[category API, AMS 18 19]
lemma IsSObj.comp {m n : SimplexCategory} (θ : m ⟶ n) {F : Arrow (Fin (n.len + 1)) ⥤ A}
    (hF : IsSObj P F) : IsSObj P (θ.toOrderHom.monotone.functor.mapArrow ⋙ F) where
  prop _ := hF.prop _
  isZero i := hF.isZero (θ.toOrderHom i)
  shortExact _ _ _ hij hjk :=
    hF.shortExact _ _ _ (θ.toOrderHom.monotone hij) (θ.toOrderHom.monotone hjk)

/-- Waldhausen's `S_•`-construction of `P`, as a simplicial category: `S_n P` is the full
subcategory of `Ar[n] ⥤ A` on the objects satisfying `IsSObj P`, and a monotone map
`θ : [m] → [n]` acts by precomposition with the induced functor `Ar[m] ⥤ Ar[n]`. -/
def sConstruction : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ ⥤ Cat where
  obj n := Cat.of (sProp P n.unop).FullSubcategory
  map θ := Functor.toCatHom <| (sProp P _).lift ((sProp P _).ι ⋙
    (Functor.whiskeringLeft _ _ A).obj θ.unop.toOrderHom.monotone.functor.mapArrow)
    (fun F => F.2.comp P θ.unop)
  map_id _ := rfl
  map_comp _ _ := rfl

end SConstruction

/- ### The K-theory space and the K-groups -/

/-- The core (the groupoid of isomorphisms) of a category, as a functor `Cat ⥤ Cat`. -/
def coreFunctor : Cat.{v, u} ⥤ Cat.{v, u} where
  obj C := Cat.of (Core C)
  map F := F.toFunctor.core.toCatHom
  map_id _ := rfl
  map_comp _ _ := rfl

/-- The diagonal simplicial set of a bisimplicial set. -/
def diagonal (B : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ ⥤ SSet.{u}) : SSet.{u} :=
  Functor.diag _ ⋙ Functor.uncurry.obj B

section KTheory

variable {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] (P : ObjectProperty A)

/-- The diagonal of the bisimplicial set `N_• iS_• P`, whose `(n, k)`-simplices are strings of
`k` composable isomorphisms in `S_n P`. -/
def kSimplicialSet : SSet := diagonal (sConstruction P ⋙ coreFunctor ⋙ nerveFunctor)

/-- The geometric realization `|iS_• P|`. Waldhausen's K-theory space of `P` is the loop space
of this space. -/
noncomputable def kSpace : TopCat := SSet.toTop.obj (kSimplicialSet P)

/-- The object of `S_0 P` given by the constant functor at the zero object. -/
noncomputable def zeroSObj (hP : P 0) : (sProp P ⦋0⦌).FullSubcategory where
  obj := (Functor.const _).obj 0
  property :=
    { prop := fun _ => hP
      isZero := fun _ => isZero_zero A
      shortExact := fun _ _ _ _ _ => ⟨(isZero_zero A).eq_of_src _ _,
        { exact := ShortComplex.exact_of_isZero_X₂ _ (isZero_zero A)
          mono_f := by dsimp; infer_instance
          epi_g := by dsimp; infer_instance }⟩ }

/-- The base point of `kSpace P`: the vertex given by the zero object. -/
noncomputable def kBasepoint (hP : P 0) : kSpace P :=
  TopCat.toSSetObjEquiv _ _
    ((sSetTopAdj.unit.app (kSimplicialSet P)).app (Opposite.op ⦋0⦌)
      (ComposableArrows.mk₀ (Core.mk (zeroSObj P hP))))
    ⟨_, ite_eq_mem_stdSimplex ℝ (0 : Fin 1)⟩

/-- The `i`-th K-group `K_i P = π_{i+1}(|iS_• P|, ∗)` of `P`, where `∗` is the vertex given by
the zero object. -/
noncomputable abbrev KGroup (hP : P 0) (i : ℕ) : Type _ :=
  π_ (i + 1) (kSpace P) (kBasepoint P hP)

end KTheory

/- ### Vector bundles and the algebraic K-theory of a scheme -/

section VectorBundles

variable (X : Scheme.{u})

/-- A sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules `M` is a vector bundle (i.e. locally free of finite rank) if
every point has an open neighbourhood `U` such that the restriction of `M` to `U` is
isomorphic to a free `𝒪_U`-module of some finite rank `n`. -/
def IsVectorBundle (M : X.Modules) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : X, ∃ (U : X.Opens) (n : ℕ), x ∈ U ∧
    Nonempty (M.restrict U.ι ≅
      SheafOfModules.free (R := (U : Scheme.{u}).ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin n)))

/-- The zero sheaf is a vector bundle (of rank `0`). -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem isVectorBundle_zero : IsVectorBundle X 0 :=
  fun _ => ⟨⊤, 0, trivial, ⟨IsZero.iso
    ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor _).map_isZero (isZero_zero _))
    ((isColimitEquivIsInitialOfIsEmpty _ (colimit.cocone _) (colimit.isColimit _)).isZero)⟩⟩

/-- The `i`-th algebraic K-group `K_i(X)` of a scheme `X`, defined as the `i`-th K-group of the
exact category of vector bundles on `X` (with base point the zero vector bundle). -/
noncomputable abbrev algebraicKGroup (i : ℕ) : Type _ :=
  KGroup (IsVectorBundle X) (isVectorBundle_zero X) i

end VectorBundles

/-- A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` is projective if it factors as a closed immersion
`X ⟶ ℙ^n_S` followed by the projection `ℙ^n_S ⟶ S`, for some `n`. -/
def IsProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (g : X ⟶ ℙ(Fin (n + 1); S)),
    IsClosedImmersion g ∧ CategoryStruct.comp g (pullback.fst _ _) = f

/-- Projective space `ℙ^n_S` is projective over `S`. -/
@[category test, AMS 14]
lemma isProjective_projectiveSpace {S : Scheme.{u}} (n : ℕ) :
    IsProjective (pullback.fst _ _ : ℙ(Fin (n + 1); S) ⟶ S) :=
  ⟨n, 𝟙 _, inferInstance, Category.id_comp _⟩

/-- The higher K-groups `K_i(X)`, `i ≥ 1`, are abelian groups. -/
@[category test, AMS 19]
noncomputable example (X : Scheme.{u}) (i : ℕ) : CommGroup (algebraicKGroup X (i + 1)) :=
  inferInstance

/--
**Parshin's conjecture.** Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety over a finite field $k$.
Then the higher algebraic K-groups of $X$ vanish up to torsion: for every $i > 0$,
$K_i(X) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = 0$, i.e. every element of $K_i(X)$ has finite order.

Here a variety over $k$ is an integral scheme `X` with a morphism `f : X ⟶ Spec k`; it is
smooth (resp. projective) if `f` is. Since `K_i(X)` is an abelian group, `Monoid.IsTorsion`
is equivalent to $K_i(X) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = 0$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 14 19]
theorem parshins_conjecture (k : Type u) [Field k] [Finite k] (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X]
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsSmooth f] (hf : IsProjective f) (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
    Monoid.IsTorsion (algebraicKGroup X i) := by
  sorry

end ParshinsConjecture

items: Higher algebraic K-groups are defined via Waldhausen's S_•-construction applied to the exact category of vector bundles Vect(X) ⊆ 𝒪_X-Mod (exact structure = short exact sequences of sheaves of 𝒪_X-modules with all three terms vector bundles), with weak equivalences the isomorphisms: K_i(X) := π_{i+1}(|N_• iS_• Vect(X)|, ∗). This agrees with Quillen's K-theory of the exact category Vect(X) by Waldhausen's comparison theorem, and with modern definitions (Thomason–Trobaugh) since X is projective over a field (has an ample line bundle). Reviewers should check the S_n-object condition (`IsSObj`): all F(i,j) satisfy P, F(i,i) is a zero object, F(i,j) → F(i,k) → F(j,k) short exact for all i ≤ j ≤ k; the simplicial structure is precomposition along Ar[θ].

The K-theory space is the realization of the diagonal of the bisimplicial set (n,k) ↦ N_k(iS_n P); its homotopy groups are those of the bisimplicial realization. The base point is the vertex given by the zero object of S_0 (constant functor at 0); this requires the API lemma `isVectorBundle_zero` (proved, no sorry). `∗` is canonical; |iS_•P| is connected so the choice does not matter mathematically.

'Vanish up to torsion' (K_i(X) ⊗ ℚ = 0) is rendered as `Monoid.IsTorsion (algebraicKGroup X i)`, i.e. every element has finite order; these are equivalent for abelian groups (π_{i+1} with i+1 ≥ 2 is abelian). 'Higher' K-groups means i > 0 (`0 < i`), as in the Wikipedia article (K_i(X) ⊗ ℚ = 0 for i > 0).

'Smooth projective variety over a finite field k' is modeled as: `[Field k] [Finite k]`, `X : Scheme` with `[IsIntegral X]`, a morphism `f : X ⟶ Spec k` with Mathlib's `[IsSmooth f]` and a bespoke `IsProjective f` (f factors as a closed immersion into ℙ^n_S := `ProjectiveSpace (Fin (n+1)) S` from FormalConjecturesForMathlib followed by the projection `pullback.fst`). Separatedness and finite type follow from projectivity. Including `IsIntegral X` matches the usual meaning of 'variety'; dropping it gives an equivalent conjecture since a smooth projective k-scheme is a finite disjoint union of integral ones and K-theory is additive.

Vector bundle = locally free of finite rank: every point has an open neighbourhood U with `M.restrict U.ι ≅ SheafOfModules.free (ULift (Fin n))` over the open subscheme U (rank may vary between components, which is harmless).

The category-theoretic composition `≫` is written `CategoryStruct.comp` in `IsProjective` because the repository globally overloads `≫` with an asymptotics notation (FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Analysis/Asymptotics/Basic.lean).
Universe choices: k : Type u and X : Scheme.{u}; the K-theory constructions are universe polymorphic over the abelian category A.

reviewer_notes: Ambiguities: (1) 'variety' is read as an integral scheme (IsIntegral X) with smooth projective structure morphism; dropping IsIntegral would give an equivalent conjecture (a smooth projective k-scheme is a finite disjoint union of such varieties, and K-theory of a disjoint union is a product). (2) 'K-groups of X' are Quillen's K-groups of the exact category of vector bundles, defined via Waldhausen's S-construction (K_i = π_{i+1}|iS_•|, realization of the diagonal of the bisimplicial nerve); F(i,i) is required to be *a* zero object rather than a fixed one, which yields a levelwise equivalent simplicial category and hence the same homotopy type. (3) 'Vanish up to torsion' = every element has finite order (Monoid.IsTorsion), equivalent to K_i(X) ⊗ ℚ = 0 for abelian groups. Bail-outs c02/c05/c06/c07 argued that higher K-theory cannot be defined without substantial infrastructure; the shipped file supplies exactly that infrastructure from Mathlib primitives (abelian category X.Modules, ShortComplex.ShortExact, Core, nerve, geometric realization, homotopy groups), with no placeholders, so the omission reason does not hold. Mathlib's IsSmooth (locally standard smooth) is the standard notion of smooth morphism. The final file compiles with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning.
